title: Feeling versus showing off in traditional jazz
summary: Barnes contrasts traditional jazz, played to move the audience, with Dixieland and bop, which he says show off.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Because the Dixieland music don't use traditional jazz at all. They start the band off right on four and on the cymbal you see, cha cha cha cha cha cha you don't have to be that sound about before. That's the Dixieland. They start that. But traditional jazz you weren't allowed to play, a new drum player wasn't allowed to jump on the cymbal when you start off. He had to play that snare drum. See they used to work plenty on the snare drum. It was very beautiful. And it's traditional jazz music, that's music that shakes you up more than any music. Yeah. Well you get quite a beat shaken out of Dixieland but that's the last part of it. When you play in Dixieland there's nothing to go to. But when you play traditional jazz, when you get to the last, then you jump to that four beat and it changes like another band coming. Can you get me? Yeah, I think I understand. And it would give you great inspiration. You get to the music and people get to shout. Yeah. It's quite different from bop and rock and roll because when you play bop music people sit down and listen, but when you're playing traditional jazz you can't sit so easy. Your feet's going or something. Yeah that's true.
It's something, if you have a little baby in there, the little baby will start dancing. I know.

And traditional jazz, most of the musicians don't be jumping around with the instruments, showing off and all that. They be straight trying to make you feel good. Traditional jazz is to make you get the feeling. Where the Dixland band come in, they want to make the people see how good they are.
Oh I see. So they show off.

Yeah. Like bop, they show off. They do the instruments, throw the instruments back ahead and do all kinds of things. You know, a real show that the people are not interested in the music, look how great I am, look what I can do with my instrument. See a traditional band is not that traditional jazz. It is to play to make you get the fire and inspiration. You don't be jumping around but be playing so hot that you can't keep still. You grab some, you call this dance, you know? And that's the difference. Anything else you want to ask me?
